purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five individually registered Dublin City NIAH buildings

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.note: Official national CSV coordinate fields are ITM, latitude and longitude. Individual NIAH webpage coordinate pairs are preserved separately as raw unlabelled-CRS evidence.

candidate_records.name: Amberley House
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010187 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1840, with two-storey over-basement return. Built as one of a pair with No.33 (50010186); both were recently restored and extended according to the NIAH record. Yellow Flemish-bond brick, granite plinth, calp-stone basement, gauged openings, timber sliding sashes, wrought-iron balconettes and Ionic doorcase. Rear return abuts modern four-storey brick mews development shared with adjoining house. NIAH appraisal notes restored interior plasterwork, ceiling roses, original decorative timber joinery and dog-leg stair.

candidate_records.name: Irish Print Union/Marine Port and General Workers Group (SIPTU)
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010188 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1840. Painted Flemish-bond brick on painted granite plinth, gauged brick window openings, round-headed door opening with Ionic doorcase, granite platform and steps with partially intact cast-iron bootscraper, decorative railings and basement gate. Two-storey yellow-brick former coach house to rear. NIAH appraisal notes loss of windows but survival of doorcase, decorative ironmongery and overall Georgian composition.

candidate_records.name: Avondale Bed and Breakfast
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010193 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1820, with three-storey extension rising from original two-storey return. NIAH records yellow Flemish-bond brick, granite plinth, Ionic doorcase, original petal fanlight, shared granite platform, cast-iron bootscraper, six granite steps and decorative railings. Appraisal describes the house as built as one of a pair and currently interconnected with its pair; preserve the registered building identity and document interconnection as a relationship, not as a merged object.

duplicate_screen.method: Exact registration-number searches against open repository issues and pull requests.
duplicate_screen.result: No open issue or pull request matches returned for any of the five exact registration numbers at time of research.

identity_and_coordinate_cautions: No.34 (50010187) is the registered pair to No.33 (50010186); keep distinct registrations and retain the pair relationship.

Nos.38 and 39 (50010191 and 50010192) are separately registered houses built as a pair, with shared hostel use, shared granite platform and basement access features described by NIAH. Do not merge the building registrations or create unsupported extra objects for shared features.

No.40 (50010193) is described as built as one of a pair and interconnected at survey time; verify the adjoining identity from its own registration before asserting a pair relationship in any future catalogue record.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs have no stated CRS; do not reinterpret them as EPSG:2157 or substitute them for CSV coordinates.
NIAH use and condition descriptions are survey-time source statements, not present-day verification. No access, ownership or current condition has been verified.
explicitly_not_done: No source registry or visual inventory imports
